facts.title: Martiros Saryan
facts.text: Born on the banks of the Don, he established himself as the father of modern Armenian painting.
His first trip to Armenia revealed to him the luminous beauty of his ancestral homeland.
In Etchmiadzin, he aided genocide survivors alongside Hovhannes Tumanyan.

facts.title: Builder of Institutions
facts.text: Settled in Yerevan, he designed Soviet Armenia's coat of arms with Hakob Kojoyan.

facts.title: The Tragedy of the Phrygie
facts.text: The ship carrying his paintings caught fire, destroying much of his Parisian work.

facts.title: “Painter of Happiness”
facts.text: In 1960, Aragon praised the painter of happiness whose canvases reveal Armenia's light to the world.
Laid to rest near Komitas, his portrait is engraved in Yerevan on the 20,000-dram banknote.

ytTitle: Martiros Saryan, the Master Who Painted the Soul and Light of Armenia
ytLead: Father of modern Armenian painting, Martiros Saryan captured the radiant light of his ancestral land. A cultural builder in Yerevan, his luminous oeuvre endures in the pantheon of giants.
